Ruling: batch #230 item 1 · letter F · maintainer 「同意 F」 2026-09-28T02:50Z

Director seat (objectstack#12708, summon #30 续 2, `session_01AsCNgFBs8HCjwhyHQsFbx3`). Provenance: maintainer, live PM chat with the director seat, 2026-09-28, replying to batch #230 (this card, item 1, recommendation F) after a business-level walk-through of what F does; verbatim 「同意 F」.

**Ruled: F.** A grouped grid over a data source that declares no `queryGroupHeaders` refuses grouping loudly, and the Partial marker is retired everywhere. Grouping is a property of the query (ruling A on objectui#7189, `5509036555`); a source that cannot answer the group-header query cannot group, and the grid names the missing member instead of grouping the page it fetched. K (keep page grouping with the marker) is not taken.

Readings that decided it:
- Long-term: one mode. The client-side page-grouping path is the interim state ruling A named, not the contract; K would keep it alive beside the server path.
- AI-safety: F fails at render time and names the missing capability. K's disclosure holds only on a grid that owns its fetch — a grouped grid mounted through `ListView` over such a source receives a window with no total and renders page-sliced counts with no marker (PR #10878 review, `5862150828`, item 5).
- Real use: every grouped view in the repo rides the objectstack adapter, which answers the header query; no in-repo or named external consumer groups a grid over `ApiDataSource`, `ValueDataSource` or a host adapter. Retirement is immediate — no window, no staged period.
- Mainstream (from memory, not re-read): AG Grid offers row grouping on its client-side model (all rows present) and its server-side model (the server supplies the groups), and not on its paged infinite model; Airtable and Notion compute group-by over the whole view on the server. None ships "group the current page and mark it partial" as a contract.

Execution parameters (ruled in the same stroke; no further decision card):
- Lane `domain:ui`; this card is the work card, re-queued; `priority:p3`. Semver `minor` with the breaking semantics stated in the changeset (never `major`, per objectui `AGENTS.md`).
- Scope: (1) `ObjectGrid` — a grouped grid that owns its fetch over a source without `queryGroupHeaders` renders an error panel naming that member, and issues no row query, instead of fetching a window and bucketing it. (2) `ListView` — makes the same refusal before mounting a grouped grid over such a source, since today it hands the grid a window as `data` (`hasInlineData`), which the grid would group as if the rows were whole. (3) Retire the Partial marker: `grid.grouping.partialBadge` / `partialNotice` / `partialNoticeUnknownTotal` in `ObjectGrid` and the ten locale rows, `groupedPartialDisclosure-7189.test.tsx`, and the "two cases still group in the browser" docs section rewritten to: rows handed in whole group where they are; everything else needs the header query. (4) The pending `.changeset/7189-grouped-grid-partial-disclosure.md` carries the dated note the #10878 review asked for (③), unless PR #10878 already added it.
- Kept: rows handed in whole (`hasInlineData` from a page schema or a parent view) still group in the browser, exactly; `useGroupedData` stays for that case.
- Out of scope, named so the dev does not refuse it: a `ListView` over the objectstack adapter while a toolbar search is active still hands a window and groups it page-sliced; that path waits on objectstack#20358 (the aggregate branch drops `search`), not on this card.
- `ValueDataSource` does not gain `queryGroupHeaders` here; when a consumer appears it can implement the member exactly in memory.
- Pins: a grid with `grouping` over a `find`-only source renders the refusal and issues no row query; a `ListView` over the same source does the same; a grid with inline rows still groups with exact counts; a control that no locale carries a `grid.grouping.partial*` key.

State: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `domain:ui` and `priority:p3` added; the Ruled line goes on the body in the same stroke. PR #10878 (landed K as the status quo) is unaffected and lands as reviewed.

2. `ListView` makes the same refusal before mounting a grouped grid over such a source.
3. The Partial marker is retired:
   - the `grid.grouping.partial*` keys in `ObjectGrid`;
   - the ten locale rows in `packages/i18n/src/locales/*.ts`;
   - `groupedPartialDisclosure-7189.test.tsx`;
   - the docs section that says two cases still group in the browser.
4. The dated note on `.changeset/7189-grouped-grid-partial-disclosure.md`, unless PR objectui#10878 already added it.

Pins as ruled. One `minor` changeset with the breaking semantics stated.

Kept, as ruled: rows handed in whole still group in the browser (`useGroupedData`). Out of scope, as ruled: the ListView toolbar-search window (objectstack#20358), and `ValueDataSource` gaining the member.

Stop on breach; explain in the report.
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` (TIER_DEFAULT, objectstack `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs:12692` at `c5dcb3ba`)
Clause-②: yes
Why yes (narrowing): a published component that grouped the fetched page over any source now refuses grouping over a source without `queryGroupHeaders`. That narrows what a document can do, so a contract review is owed before landing.

Serial constraints cleared: read 2026-09-28T03:10Z at objectui `origin/main` `b2683a2c0`.
- PR objectui#10878 (objectui#7189, option K) merged, which this card builds on.
- The only open PR on these files is PR objectui#10278 (`Part of #9853`, draft, another seat), in `ObjectGrid.tsx`. Triage's answer `5861161215` on objectui#7189 flipped that order: objectui#9853 is `pm:on-hold` on an unreleased `@objectstack/spec`, so the grouping line goes ahead, and PR objectui#10278 merges `main` after it. This card follows that order. The dev still maps PR objectui#10278's hunks and avoids lines it holds where the ruled change allows, listing any it must touch.
- No open PR touches `ListView.tsx`, the locales, the docs page or the changeset.

## ACCEPT — PR objectui#10896 · `domain:ui` seat #1 · 2026-09-28T05:28Z

`session_01DuWo5bdP9SdVebamn99GGk` (`os-steve`), the dispatching seat and reviewer of record. Checked against GitHub and `origin/main`, ⛔ not against the reports.

**Checklist**
- **Shape.** Draft → `main`. The body opens `Fixes #10881`, the only closing keyword, and `Clause-②: yes` sits at line start. PR assignee `os-steve`.
- **Scope.** 39 files, +1110 / −772. Ruling F (`5862401217`) executed as ruled:
  1. `ObjectGrid` over a source without `queryGroupHeaders` refuses grouping in the load-error panel idiom (`role="alert"`, naming the member) and issues no row query.
  2. `ListView` makes the same refusal and never mounts the grid.
  3. The Partial marker is retired everywhere: the three keys in the grid defaults and the ten packs, the notice, `GroupRow`'s partial label, the pin file, and the docs section, rewritten as ruled.
  4. Dated notes on the two 7189 changesets.
  5. One `minor` changeset for `@object-ui/plugin-grid`, `@object-ui/plugin-list` and `@object-ui/i18n`, with the breaking semantics and the migration.

  Rows handed in whole still group exactly (`useGroupedData`), as ruled.
- **Decided by this seat, reversed once, recorded here (execution, ⛔ not escalated): B.** The dev asked about a host that hands a grouped grid rows AND declares them one page of more (external manual pagination with a larger `rowCount`). The seat first answered A (leave it).
  - The contract review measured that A regressed a case PR objectui#10878 disclosed: 100 of 186 rows drew two groups with three units missing and no notice.
  - The ruling keeps only rows handed in WHOLE, so the seat reversed to B.
  - The grid refuses that declared window with its own key, `grid.grouping.needsWholeRows`, in all ten packs, even over a capable source, since the host owns the fetch there.
  - No refusal when `rowCount` is absent or equal to the rows (pinned controls).
  - `ListView` was measured never to hand a grouped grid host paging (pinned, with a lit ungrouped control).
- **Governed-surface predicate.** 39 paths: `NOT governed` (AGENTS.md lit control: exit 3).
- **Checks on head `94df46014`.** 43 check-runs: 40 success, 3 skipped, 0 failure. `mergeable_state` clean.
- **Contract review.**
  - **Round 1:** record `5863494567` on `638a8250c` was a **PASS**, with ③ flags: A's reasoning, the refusal flash, the lost card-view pin, and a changeset understatement.
  - **Patch round 2** (`94df46014`) took all of them:
    - B;
    - the header-query panel after the spinner branch, so no error flash;
    - the card-view exclusion re-homed as a behavioural pin;
    - the changeset naming rows handed in whole.

    The seat applied the dev's r2 body through the relay, read back identical.

    - traced `hostRowCount`'s only two read sites;
    - checked the render order after the reorder;
    - found `git merge-tree` onto current `main` clean.

**Out-of-scope findings, one line each (Acceptance notes)**
- PR objectui#10278 (another seat, `pm:on-hold` on an unreleased spec) will meet two `ObjectGrid.tsx` regions and the docs when it merges `main`. Triage `5861161215` set this order. Its docs sentence about a grouped view fetching a larger batch no longer describes the grid.

- A masked-only grouping key over a host-DECLARED window shows the whole-rows refusal until the object definition lands. There is no in-repo producer. No card.
- The i18n pin's presence control does not list `needsWholeRows`; the key-parity gates cover it and are green.
- The round-1 commits carry the harness-written trailer. It does not reach `main`: the squash message is the PR title plus body.
